## Introduction and overview {#intro}

  ----------------------- --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
  Module                  Multimodal Generative AI
  Code                    CSC_52002_EP

  Period                  Autumn semester · period 2 (from 04/01/2027 to 19/03/2027) · X3A session "Multimodal Generative AI" (code X3A LU3); course taught in English

**Audience**: an engineer who knows a CNN / autoencoder and wants to generate or align text×image. **Empirical first**: a VAE that reconstructs blurry (β too low); a GAN that mode-collapses after 20 k steps; a CLIP whose retrieval drops as soon as the domain leaves the web — then we name ELBO, diffusion, guidance.

VAE, GAN, diffusion, CLIP and text-to-image. Bridge to neural rendering and generative control in M2.

### What you will be able to do

-   Derive and train a VAE: ELBO, reparameterization, latent spaces and their properties.
-   Explain adversarial GAN training, its equilibria and instabilities, and the contribution of the Wasserstein variant.
-   Describe generation by diffusion: DDPM and score matching, and the link between the two viewpoints.
-   Use guidance (notably classifier-free), accelerated sampling (DDIM) and latent diffusion.
-   Understand CLIP and the alignment of vision-language spaces that makes text-to-image possible.
-   Assemble the complete text-to-image pipeline and identify the role of each component.
-   Explain how video, audio and robot actions are generated with the same latent-diffusion and token-modeling recipes (video DiT, codec tokens, diffusion policies, VLA models).
-   Situate the further extensions of generation: 3D, multimodal LLMs and world models.
-   Evaluate generative models (notably with FID), estimate their computational costs and discuss their ethical issues.

### Official objectives and syllabus (2026-2027 catalog)

The official 2026–2027 sheet (French title "IA générative multimodale", scheduled session "Multimodal Generative AI", period X-3A-P2, from 04/01/2027 to 19/03/2027, taught in English) carries a two-paragraph description in English.

Generative AI lets machines interpret and process data through several modalities and sensors — vision, audio, touch — and its multimodal development is presented as both a major scientific advance and a paradigm shift for industries from healthcare to automotive, with tools such as Dall-E 3, Midjourney and GPT-Vision building on large vision models, and autonomous-driving companies expanding. The class announces that it goes beyond CNNs and transformers to the advanced topics of multimodal generative AI: "from image to video generation, sound, robot actions".

Nothing else is displayed: no teaching volume, no prerequisites, no assessment modality, no programme.

### Where this course fits in the program

Module of period 2 of M1 (teaching volume not displayed on the 2026–2027 sheet; 36 h and 4.5 ECTS per the LLGA curriculum wiki): an option explicitly **recommended for the LLGA track**, of which Xi Wang is the official head ("responsable" on the 2026–2027 sheet). Official prerequisites: not displayed on the sheet. This is where the master's program shifts from learning representations to multimodal generation.

-   **Prerequisites** — [Deep Learning](../m1p1-deep-learning/index.html) for architectures and training (the review section covers probabilities, networks and the ELBO, hence VAEs and GANs); the [Signal Processing](../m1p1-signal-processing/index.html) module is useful for the signal and spectrogram processing mobilized by the audio and video extensions.
-   **Downstream modules** — it directly grounds [Control in Generative AI](../m2-control-generative-ai/index.html) (M2), which teaches how to steer these generative models; it prepares [Advanced Topics in Large Language Models](../m2-advanced-topics-llms/index.html) (M2) for multimodal LLMs, and [Speech Technology for Conversational AI](../m2-speech-technology/index.html) (M2) for speech generation.

### Course outline

-   **Review: probabilities, networks, ELBO** — the probabilistic and neural foundation reactivated before the generative models.
-   **VAEs and latent spaces** — encoding and decoding with a distribution: the first generative building block.
-   **GANs: adversary, equilibrium, Wasserstein** — learning through a game between generator and discriminator.
-   **Diffusion: DDPM and score matching** — denoising progressively: the paradigm that dominates generation.
-   **Guidance, DDIM and latent diffusion** — controlling generation, speeding it up and making it computationally affordable.
-   **CLIP and vision-language alignment** — the common space where text and image meet.
-   **Text-to-image: the complete pipeline** — assembling tokenizer, latent space, diffusion and decoder.
-   **Evaluation, costs, ethics** — measuring quality (FID among others), weighing costs, questioning uses.
-   **Beyond images: video, sound, robot actions, 3D, multimodal LLMs** — the modalities named by the official description, then the current frontiers.
-   **Course research notes (Kalogeiton et al.)** — a tour of the research work related to the course (self-study).
-   **Exercises** and **References** — systematic training and sources to go further.

### How to study this module

-   Start with the review section and make sure you can derive the ELBO: VAEs, and later latent diffusion, collapse without it.
-   Train a small VAE on a simple dataset before tackling GANs: the contrast between the two ways of learning to generate is very instructive.
-   For each model, write down in black and white the loss function and the sampling algorithm: in generative modeling, these two lines summarize everything.
-   Follow the thread of latent spaces: VAEs, then latent diffusion, then CLIP form a progression, not three independent chapters.
-   Take this module alongside [Machine learning with Optimal Transport and Algorithmic Fairness](../m1p2-optimal-transport/index.html) (same period): the Wasserstein distance, the Wasserstein-GAN and the FID illuminate one another there.
-   Redo the exercises of each section before moving on to the next, and keep the chapter on evaluation, costs and ethics as a critical reading grid for everything else.
